ai_root_cause: PC1 is addressed 10.10.10.11/255.255.255.0, which belongs to VLAN 10 (SVI 10.10.10.1), but its switch port is in VLAN 20. The host is in the wrong broadcast domain.
ai_evidence: Access Mode VLAN: 20 (GUEST) || Vlan10                 10.10.10.1      YES manual up                    up || IP Address......................: 10.10.10.11
ai_fix_steps: conf t | interface <port> | switchport access vlan <correct-id> | end | Verify: show vlan brief places the port in the right VLAN and the host pings its gateway
ai_risk_note: Moving an access port between VLANs flushes that port's MAC entries and will briefly interrupt any other device on it.
expected_fault: Access port Fa0/1 is assigned to VLAN 20 (GUEST) instead of VLAN 10 (STAFF)

ai_root_cause: An access port is assigned to VLAN 30 but the switch reports it as Inactive, meaning the VLAN was never created in the VLAN database. All frames for that VLAN are dropped.
ai_evidence: Access Mode VLAN: 30 (Inactive) || Fa0/10                       connected    30         a-full a-100 10/100BaseTX || Fa0/11                       connected    30         a-full a-100 10/100BaseTX || Fa0/12                       connected    30         a-full a-100 10/100BaseTX
ai_fix_steps: conf t | vlan <id> | name <NAME> | end | Verify: show vlan brief lists the VLAN as active with its member ports
ai_risk_note: Moving an access port between VLANs flushes that port's MAC entries and will briefly interrupt any other device on it.
expected_fault: VLAN 30 is referenced by the access ports but does not exist in the VLAN database

ai_root_cause: VLAN 20 (GUEST) is active on SW1 with member ports Fa0/4, Fa0/5, but it is not in the allowed VLAN list on trunk Gi0/1. Traffic for that VLAN works locally and fails across the trunk.
ai_evidence: Gi0/1       on           802.1q         trunking      1 || 20   GUEST                            active    Fa0/4, Fa0/5
ai_fix_steps: conf t | interface <trunk-port> | switchport trunk allowed vlan add <id> | end | Verify: show interfaces trunk lists the VLAN as allowed and active
ai_risk_note: Editing an allowed-VLAN list with 'switchport trunk allowed vlan <list>' replaces the list. Always use 'add' unless you intend to overwrite it.
expected_fault: VLAN 20 is missing from the allowed VLAN list on the SW1 trunk Gi0/1

ai_root_cause: The two ends of the trunk disagree on the native VLAN ([1, 99]). Untagged frames are placed in different VLANs on each side, merging the broadcast domains and creating a VLAN-hopping exposure.
ai_evidence: %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1 (99), with SW2 GigabitEthernet0/1 (1). || Gi0/1       on           802.1q         trunking      99 || Gi0/1       on           802.1q         trunking      1
ai_fix_steps: conf t | interface <trunk-port> | switchport trunk native vlan <agreed-id> | end | Verify: both ends report the same native VLAN and the CDP mismatch log stops
ai_risk_note: Editing an allowed-VLAN list with 'switchport trunk allowed vlan <list>' replaces the list. Always use 'add' unless you intend to overwrite it.
expected_fault: 802.1Q native VLAN mismatch across the trunk: VLAN 99 on SW1 versus VLAN 1 on SW2

ai_root_cause: SW1 Gi0/1 reports 'not-trunking'. The far end is most likely a static access port or the encapsulation/mode pair cannot be negotiated, so only untagged VLAN 1 traffic crosses the link.
ai_evidence: Gi0/1       on           802.1q         not-trunking  1
ai_fix_steps: conf t | interface <port> | switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q | switchport mode trunk | end | Verify: show interfaces trunk reports Status trunking on both ends
ai_risk_note: Editing an allowed-VLAN list with 'switchport trunk allowed vlan <list>' replaces the list. Always use 'add' unless you intend to overwrite it.
expected_fault: SW2 Gi0/1 is a static access port, so the 802.1Q trunk never negotiates

ai_root_cause: SW3 GigabitEthernet0/2 is administratively down (shutdown). Every VLAN, subinterface or route that depends on it is unreachable.
ai_evidence: GigabitEthernet0/2     unassigned      YES unset  administratively down down
ai_fix_steps: conf t | interface <interface> | no shutdown | end | Verify: show ip interface brief reports the interface up/up
ai_risk_note: Editing an allowed-VLAN list with 'switchport trunk allowed vlan <list>' replaces the list. Always use 'add' unless you intend to overwrite it.
expected_fault: Uplink trunk GigabitEthernet0/2 is administratively down (shutdown)

ai_root_cause: R1 GigabitEthernet0/0.20 has an IP address but no 'encapsulation dot1Q' statement. Without a VLAN tag binding, the subinterface line protocol stays down and that VLAN has no Layer 3 gateway.
ai_evidence: interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20 || ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0 || GigabitEthernet0/0.20      192.168.20.1    YES manual up                    down
ai_fix_steps: conf t | interface <subinterface> | encapsulation dot1Q <vlan> | ip address <ip> <mask> | end | Verify: the subinterface is up/up and hosts in that VLAN ping their gateway
ai_risk_note: Bouncing a parent interface takes every subinterface down with it, so schedule it outside production hours.
expected_fault: Subinterface Gi0/0.20 is missing its 'encapsulation dot1Q 20' statement

ai_root_cause: R1 GigabitEthernet0/0 is administratively down (shutdown). Every VLAN, subinterface or route that depends on it is unreachable. Its subinterfaces GigabitEthernet0/0.10, GigabitEthernet0/0.20, GigabitEthernet0/0.30 inherit the shutdown state.
ai_evidence: GigabitEthernet0/0         unassigned      YES manual administratively down down
ai_fix_steps: conf t | interface <interface> | no shutdown | end | Verify: show ip interface brief reports the interface up/up
ai_risk_note: Bouncing a parent interface takes every subinterface down with it, so schedule it outside production hours.
expected_fault: Physical interface Gi0/0 is shut down, which takes every dot1Q subinterface down with it

ai_root_cause: 'show ip route' returned 'Default gateway is not set' instead of a routing table while SVIs with IP addresses exist. The global 'ip routing' command is missing, so the switch will not forward packets between VLANs.
ai_evidence: Default gateway is not set || Vlan10                 192.168.10.1    YES manual up                    up || Vlan20                 192.168.20.1    YES manual up                    up
ai_fix_steps: conf t | ip routing | end | Verify: show ip route now displays connected routes for every SVI subnet
ai_risk_note: Bouncing a parent interface takes every subinterface down with it, so schedule it outside production hours.
expected_fault: IP routing is disabled on the multilayer switch ('ip routing' is absent)

ai_root_cause: PC-STAFF-7 is 192.168.10.77/255.255.255.0 (network 192.168.10.0/24) but its default gateway is 192.168.1.1, which is not in that network. The host has no usable next hop for off-subnet traffic; same-subnet traffic still works via ARP.
ai_fix_steps: Open the host's IP configuration | Set the default gateway to the router address inside the host's own subnet | Verify: ipconfig shows the corrected gateway and an off-subnet ping succeeds
ai_risk_note: Confirm no server or printer depends on the address you are about to change, and update DNS and any DHCP reservation at the same time.
expected_fault: PC-STAFF-7 has the wrong default gateway (192.168.1.1 instead of 192.168.10.1)

ai_root_cause: PC-LAB-4 uses mask 255.255.255.0 while the gateway interface holding 172.16.8.1 is configured with 255.255.252.0. The host's idea of its local subnet is wrong, so some on-link destinations are sent to the router and fail.
ai_fix_steps: Open the host's IP configuration | Set the subnet mask to match the gateway interface | Verify: ipconfig shows the correct mask and all on-link hosts are reachable
ai_risk_note: Confirm no server or printer depends on the address you are about to change, and update DNS and any DHCP reservation at the same time.
expected_fault: Subnet mask mismatch on PC-LAB-4: 255.255.255.0 configured where the segment uses 255.255.252.0

ai_root_cause: 10.10.50.10 is configured on more than one device (SRV-WEB, SRV-PRINT). Both answer ARP, the ARP cache flaps between their MAC addresses and roughly half of all sessions land on the wrong host.
ai_evidence: IP Address......................: 10.10.50.10 || R3# show logging | include DUPADDR
ai_fix_steps: Identify which device was addressed most recently | Reassign that device to a free address in the subnet | clear arp-cache on the gateway | Verify: show ip arp lists exactly one MAC per IP and a sustained ping has zero loss
ai_risk_note: Confirm no server or printer depends on the address you are about to change, and update DNS and any DHCP reservation at the same time.
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address 10.10.50.10 assigned to both SRV-WEB and SRV-PRINT

ai_root_cause: R1 GigabitEthernet0/0.20 carries a client subnet but has no ip helper-address, while GigabitEthernet0/0.10 on the same router does. DHCP DISCOVER is a broadcast and cannot cross a router without a relay, so clients on GigabitEthernet0/0.20 never reach the DHCP server.
ai_evidence: interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20 || encapsulation dot1Q 20 || ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0 || IP Address......................: 169.254.201.44
ai_fix_steps: conf t | interface <client-facing-interface> | ip helper-address <dhcp-server> | end | Verify: the client renews and receives an address from the correct scope
ai_risk_note: Clearing bindings forces every client to renew at once; expect a short burst of DHCP traffic and some brief client interruptions.
expected_fault: Missing 'ip helper-address' on subinterface Gi0/0.20

ai_root_cause: Pool LAB30 hands out addresses from 192.168.20.0/24 but advertises default-router 192.168.30.1, which is not inside that network. Clients receive an address and a gateway that cannot reach each other.
ai_fix_steps: conf t | ip dhcp pool <name> | network <correct-net> <mask> | end | clear ip dhcp binding * | Verify: a renewed client receives an address in its own subnet and pings its gateway
ai_risk_note: Clearing bindings forces every client to renew at once; expect a short burst of DHCP traffic and some brief client interruptions.
expected_fault: DHCP pool LAB30 has the wrong network statement (192.168.20.0/24 instead of 192.168.30.0/24)

ai_root_cause: Every usable address in the pool is allocated, so newly booting clients get no offer and fall back to APIPA. Existing hosts keep their unexpired leases, which makes the failure look intermittent. Check the excluded-address ranges before widening the subnet.
ai_evidence: Total addresses                : 254 || Leased addresses               : 54 || Excluded addresses             : 200 || IP Address......................: 169.254.88.12
ai_fix_steps: conf t | Narrow the excluded-address range to only the static infrastructure | end | Verify: show ip dhcp pool reports free addresses and a new client gets a lease
ai_risk_note: Clearing bindings forces every client to renew at once; expect a short burst of DHCP traffic and some brief client interruptions.
expected_fault: DHCP pool LAB40 is exhausted: only 54 usable addresses remain after a 200-address exclusion

ai_root_cause: PC-STAFF-5 has DNS Server 0.0.0.0. The host cannot send a query at all, which is why access by IP address works and access by hostname fails. This is a Layer 7 fault, not a routing fault.
ai_fix_steps: Open the host's IP configuration | Set the DNS server address | Verify: nslookup resolves a known hostname and browsing by name works
ai_risk_note: Changing zone records can be cached by clients; flush the resolver cache before concluding the fix did not work.
expected_fault: No DNS server configured on the client (DNS Server is 0.0.0.0)

ai_root_cause: The resolver answered authoritatively that reports.lab.local does not exist while other names in the same zone resolve. The zone is missing an A record rather than the client or the transport being broken.
ai_evidence: *** 192.168.100.53 can't find reports.lab.local: Non-existent domain
ai_fix_steps: Open the DNS server's record table | Add the missing A record with the correct address | Save the zone | Verify: nslookup returns the address from every VLAN
ai_risk_note: Changing zone records can be cached by clients; flush the resolver cache before concluding the fix did not work.
expected_fault: The A record for reports.lab.local was never created on DNS-SRV

ai_root_cause: The routing table reports 'Gateway of last resort is not set' and contains no S* 0.0.0.0/0 entry, so every destination outside the connected subnets is dropped for want of a matching route.
ai_evidence: Gateway of last resort is not set
ai_fix_steps: conf t | ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 <isp-next-hop> | end | Verify: show ip route shows the gateway of last resort and the router pings an internet address
ai_risk_note: A default route alone does not provide internet access without NAT. Check both before declaring the fault fixed.
expected_fault: No default route configured on the edge router R1

ai_root_cause: The static route for 192.168.60.0/255.255.255.0 uses next hop 10.0.0.6, which does not fall inside any connected subnet on this router (10.0.0.0/30). The route installs and looks healthy but every packet matching it is black-holed.
ai_evidence: ip route 192.168.60.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.6 || C       10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/2
ai_fix_steps: conf t | no ip route <dest> <mask> <wrong-next-hop> | ip route <dest> <mask> <correct-next-hop> | end | Verify: show ip route lists the corrected next hop and the destination replies
ai_risk_note: A default route alone does not provide internet access without NAT. Check both before declaring the fault fixed.
expected_fault: Static route points to the wrong next hop 10.0.0.6, which does not exist on the 10.0.0.0/30 link

ai_root_cause: R1 holds an explicit static route toward the peer LAN, but R4 has only a default route and no specific route back. Return traffic follows the default path instead of the site-to-site link, which breaks sessions at the NAT boundary and produces one-way connectivity.
ai_fix_steps: conf t | ip route <peer-subnet> <mask> <link-next-hop> | end | Verify: show ip route holds an explicit route and traffic flows in both directions
ai_risk_note: A default route alone does not provide internet access without NAT. Check both before declaring the fault fixed.
expected_fault: R4 is missing explicit return routes for the HQ subnets and falls back to its default route

ai_root_cause: R1 GigabitEthernet0/0.30 (192.168.30.1) is up/up but does not appear in 'show ip ospf interface brief', so no network statement covers it. Its subnet is never advertised and remains invisible to every other router in the area.
ai_evidence: GigabitEthernet0/0.30      192.168.30.1    YES manual up                    up
ai_fix_steps: conf t | router ospf 1 | network <subnet> <wildcard> area <area> | end | Verify: the interface appears in show ip ospf interface brief and the peer learns the route
ai_risk_note: Removing a network statement withdraws the route from every router in the area. Re-add before removing, and watch for a transient reconvergence.
expected_fault: OSPF is missing a network statement for 192.168.30.0/24 on R1

ai_root_cause: The router logged a mismatched area ID from its neighbour. Both ends of a link must agree on the area before an adjacency can form, so hellos are discarded.
ai_evidence: %OSPF-4-ERRRCV: Received invalid packet: mismatched area ID from backbone area, from 10.0.0.6, GigabitEthernet0/3 || R2# show ip ospf neighbor
ai_fix_steps: conf t | router ospf 1 | no network <link> <wildcard> area <wrong> | network <link> <wildcard> area <correct> | end | Verify: show ip ospf neighbor reports the peer in FULL state
ai_risk_note: Removing a network statement withdraws the route from every router in the area. Re-add before removing, and watch for a transient reconvergence.
expected_fault: OSPF area mismatch on the R2-R3 link: area 0 on R2 versus area 1 on R3

ai_root_cause: An OSPF-enabled transit interface reports 'No Hellos (Passive interface)'. A passive interface never sends hellos, so no adjacency can form across it. This is usually 'passive-interface default' applied without exempting the link.
ai_evidence: No Hellos (Passive interface) || R1# show ip ospf neighbor
ai_fix_steps: conf t | router ospf 1 | no passive-interface <transit-interface> | end | Verify: show ip ospf neighbor reports the peer in FULL state
ai_risk_note: Removing a network statement withdraws the route from every router in the area. Re-add before removing, and watch for a transient reconvergence.
expected_fault: The transit interface Gi0/2 was left passive by 'passive-interface default', suppressing OSPF hellos

ai_root_cause: 'show ip nat statistics' on R1 lists no inside and no outside interface, so the NAT rule never fires. Private source addresses leave the router untranslated and are dropped upstream. The router's own traffic still works because it sources from the routable outside address.
ai_evidence: Total translations: 0 (0 static, 0 dynamic, 0 extended) || Outside interfaces: || Inside interfaces:
ai_fix_steps: conf t | interface <lan-interface> | ip nat inside | interface <wan-interface> | ip nat outside | end | Verify: show ip nat statistics lists both interfaces and translations appear
ai_risk_note: Clearing the translation table drops every active session through the router.
expected_fault: The 'ip nat inside' and 'ip nat outside' interface commands are missing

ai_root_cause: R1 GigabitEthernet0/0.50 serves 192.168.50.1, but ACL NAT-LAN used by 'ip nat inside source' permits only 192.168.10.0/24, 192.168.20.0/24. Traffic from that subnet is routed but never translated, so it leaves with a private source and the replies never return.
ai_evidence: GigabitEthernet0/0.50      192.168.50.1    YES manual up                    up || ip nat inside source list NAT-LAN interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload || permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255
ai_fix_steps: conf t | ip access-list standard <nat-acl> | permit <missing-subnet> <wildcard> | end | clear ip nat translation * | Verify: hosts in that subnet reach the internet and appear in show ip nat translations
ai_risk_note: Clearing the translation table drops every active session through the router.
expected_fault: The NAT ACL NAT-LAN does not permit 192.168.50.0/24

ai_root_cause: The NAT pool is fully allocated and the mapping has no 'overload' keyword, so each inside host consumes an entire public address one-to-one. Once the pool is used up every further host is denied a translation. PAT (overload) lets all hosts share one address by port.
ai_evidence: ip nat inside source list NAT-LAN pool PUBLIC-POOL || type generic, total addresses 8, allocated 8 (100%), misses 1276 || %IPNAT-4-ADDR_ALLOC_FAILURE: Address allocation failed for 192.168.10.42, pool PUBLIC-POOL might be exhausted
ai_fix_steps: conf t | no ip nat inside source list <acl> pool <pool> | ip nat inside source list <acl> pool <pool> overload | end | clear ip nat translation * | Verify: show ip nat statistics shows extended translations and misses stop rising
ai_risk_note: Clearing the translation table drops every active session through the router.
expected_fault: Dynamic NAT pool exhausted: eight public addresses shared one-to-one by sixty hosts, missing the 'overload' keyword

ai_root_cause: ACL 110 is actively dropping traffic: 'ip any any' has 2841 matches. Meanwhile 1 permit entry has zero matches, which means the traffic users expect to be allowed is not even reaching the permit lines — the ACL is applied to the wrong interface or direction, or a required protocol (DNS on UDP 53, ICMP, return traffic) was never permitted.
ai_evidence: 20 deny ip any any (2841 matches) || 10 permit tcp 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 10.10.50.0 0.0.0.255 eq www (0 matches)
ai_fix_steps: Identify the traffic being denied from the match counters | Add the required permit entries above the deny, or move the ACL to the correct interface/direction | Verify: the permit counters rise, the deny counter stops rising, and the application works
ai_risk_note: Do not remove an ACL to test connectivity on a live segment. Add a temporary permit with logging instead, and remove it once the test is done.
expected_fault: ACL 110 is applied inbound on the wrong interface, so it filters all traffic entering from VLAN 20 rather than only traffic destined to the server farm

ai_root_cause: ACL 120 is actively dropping traffic: 'ip any any' has 874 matches.
ai_evidence: 40 deny ip any any (874 matches)
ai_fix_steps: Identify the traffic being denied from the match counters | Add the required permit entries above the deny, or move the ACL to the correct interface/direction | Verify: the permit counters rise, the deny counter stops rising, and the application works
ai_risk_note: Do not remove an ACL to test connectivity on a live segment. Add a temporary permit with logging instead, and remove it once the test is done.
expected_fault: ACL 120 has no permit entry for DNS (UDP/TCP port 53), so the implicit deny drops all lookups

ai_root_cause: The access point and the client are configured with different SSID strings (CORP-WIFI, CORP_WIFI). SSIDs are case- and character-exact, so a hyphen versus underscore is enough to prevent association.
ai_evidence: SSID            : CORP-WIFI || SSID configured................: CORP_WIFI || IP Address......................: 169.254.44.9 || Passphrase      : Net$age2026!
ai_fix_steps: Open the client's wireless profile | Set the SSID to exactly match the AP, character for character | Reconnect | Verify: the AP shows the station associated and the client receives a DHCP address
ai_risk_note: Changing the SSID or passphrase disconnects every client on that WLAN, including any that are currently working.
expected_fault: SSID string and WPA2 passphrase mismatch between the access point and the client

ai_root_cause: ACL GUEST-ISOLATION exists with 3 entries, every one showing zero matches, and the interface reports no inbound or outbound access list. The policy was configured but never bound with 'ip access-group', so routing forwards the traffic the ACL was meant to stop. This is a security control failure rather than a connectivity fault.
ai_next_command: show ip interface | include access list
ai_evidence: 10 deny ip 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 10.10.50.0 0.0.0.255 (0 matches) || Inbound  access list is not set || Outgoing access list is not set
ai_fix_steps: conf t | interface <boundary-interface> | ip access-group <acl-name> in | end | Verify: show ip interface reports the ACL bound and the deny counters begin to increment
ai_risk_note: Do not remove an ACL to test connectivity on a live segment. Add a temporary permit with logging instead, and remove it once the test is done.
expected_fault: The GUEST-ISOLATION ACL exists but is not applied to any interface, so guest traffic is routed freely into the internal VLANs
